So a dark-leg fidelity claim must rest on a **pair comparison** — arrow vs arrow, dark vs light, at two thresholds — and never on an absolute box edge.
49	- **A PIXEL RUN p..q IS THE HALF-OPEN INTERVAL [p, q+1) — ITS CENTRE IS (p+q+1)/2 (R112, load-bearing calibration).** The inclusive form `(p+q)/2` shifts every centre 0.5 px left; on the mini month it produced margins **11.5 / 12.5** where the layout can only have equal ones (`Main.qml:2122-2123` sets the *same* `categoryInset` on both sides). The source broke the tie, and the half-open form then reproduced `categoryInset` = **12 / 12** exactly. **Corollary (the project's own R066/R111 convention): a GAP written as `line - last_ink_pixel` ("ink 44, line 52 => gap 8") is the inclusive form and reads 1 larger than the continuous gap.** Mixing the two forms is a 1 px error — so state which form a gap came from.
50	- **A DARK `gridLine` COMPOSITES, A LIGHT ONE DOES NOT (R113, load-bearing).** The dark separators read **59** over the weekday field 30 and **65** over the weekend tint 37 — one token, `white@0.13`, two backdrops. The light `#EDEDED` is opaque and reads 237 everywhere. => **"all separators share one tone" is a light-leg fact; a dark scan must expect two, and a differing separator tone is not a separator-tone bug until the backdrop under it is checked.**

In a rule row the only non-white pixels left of x272 are the gutter label's own ink (`238..264`). => **"does the rule reach across the gutter?" must be scanned right of the label ink, never by a whole-row `!= white` test.**

Judge alignment on unclipped bands, or on the clipped band's **identical ink x-extent**.

R110 read the weekend FIELD on dark: pure `(37,37,37)` at (1000,300) and (900,600) — the composite resolves to the documented 37. **The weekend CHIP is still UNWITNESSED — the fixture's Sat/Sun all-day columns are empty (R107).** Never claim a weekend chip backdrop was read.

Recorded, not fixed.**
57	- **A TRANSLUCENT CHIP CANNOT BE JOINED BY OVERLAP (R108, load-bearing).** `withAlpha(itemColor, 0.17)` over white is **220** and two overlapping chips stack to **191** — 11 % darker. **A join must be an opaque pre-blend (R109's `AppTheme.mix(backdrop, itemColor, a)`), after which the extension can be generous and immune to the ±1 rounding.** R109 is the confirmation: reach = 3 px measured, 4 px shipped.
58	- **THE JOINT'S 3 px IS ONE PIXEL OF SLACK IN THREE PIECES (R108, load-bearing).** A column is **119.0 px** (833/7) and draws its own 1 px separator as its **FIRST** pixel; the chips sit in a `ColumnLayout` inset `allDayBandInset: 1` ⇒ a chip is **116 px inside a 119 px column**. Joint = 2 px field (column leftover + layout rounding) + the neighbour's separator + the neighbour's own 1 px inset. **The leftover is known only to ±1 — that is what disqualifies an exact-fit margin and makes an overlapping one necessary.**
59	- **ONLY A LEFT-EXTENSION CAN HIDE A RULE (R108, load-bearing).** Each column's separator belongs to **that column's own delegate**, which is later in the RowLayout than the previous column's chips ⇒ it paints **above** them. So a right-extension can never cover the neighbour's rule; the neighbour's own chip, extending **left**, can. **R109 shipped exactly that: `Layout.leftMargin` only, never a right one.**
60	- **A CONTINUATION IS A DATE FACT; A COLUMN IS A PLACE (R109, load-bearing).** `allDayContinues()` (`:243-252`) is pure date arithmetic, so it returns `true` on column 0 for an item that started in the *previous week* — with a reach attached that would paint 4 px into the gutter with no rounding column. **Gate the reach on `allDayColumn.index > 0`.** The corner suppression (clause (a)) still reads the ungated flag.
61	- **THE ALL-DAY BAND IS CONTENT-SIZED WITH A ONE-ROW FLOOR (R106, load-bearing).** `allDayBandRows = clamp(maxItemsAcrossThe7Columns, 1, 3)`: **26 px** all-day-empty, **76** on the 3-row week. **`allDayMaxRows` (the cap, 3) and `allDayBandRows` (the drawn rows) must stay separate variables.**
62	- **OUR WEEKS START MONDAY, AND AN EXPANDED SIDEBAR SHIFTS THE DAY COLUMNS (R106, load-bearing).** With the sidebar expanded the gutter runs **221..272** and the separators sit at **272/391/510/629/748/867/986** — **pitch 119**. So **`x=577` is the 3rd day column; Thursday is 629..747 (x~690)**. The y-map is x-independent; only *horizontal* reads need the leg's sidebar state stated. **R115 note: the reference's mini month headers read `S M T W T F S` (Sunday-first) where ours read `一二三四五六日` (Monday-first) — an unfiled heading/header divergence, recorded on the dark leg. M02's seven-equal-columns and six-equal-rows clauses are unaffected.**
63	- **AN ALL-DAY-EMPTY WEEK STILL SHOWS A 26 px BAND (R106, extrapolation).** The spec says "min about 28", so the band has a floor rather than a hide.
64	- **THE REF'S SIDEBAR IS 192 px WIDE — "243px sidebar" WAS A CONFLATION (R105, load-bearing).** The 237-plane ends at **x=191**; the white hour gutter runs **192..243** and the first *day column* starts at **243**. ⇒ the reference's **main region is 192..813, centre 502.5** — and its segment's rim centre is **502.0**. **R063–R104 carried the wrong denominator ⇒ any ref-centredness number derived from "grid 243..812" must be recomputed.**
65	- **A CENTRED-IN-REGION SEGMENT IS −0.5 px ON BOTH SIDES, AND THAT IS THE CONVENTION (R105, load-bearing).**
66	- **A CAPSULE'S OUTER RADIUS IS MEASURED AGAINST ITS OWN INNER ELEMENT, NEVER IN ABSOLUTE PX (R104, load-bearing).**
67	- **AN ARC-ONLY FIT CANNOT SEPARATE r FROM y0 AND IS THEREFORE NOT AN ABSOLUTE INSTRUMENT (R104, load-bearing).** **Report the bound (11–13.5), not a point.**
68	- **A PILL'S HORIZONTAL PADDING IS MEASURED AGAINST ITS OWN SLOT, AND THE SLOTS OF A SEGMENTED CONTROL TILE (R102, load-bearing; R103).** **R103: the rule applies to both sides or the comparison is void. Correct ref slot = (228−4)/4 = 56.0.**
69	- **A WHOLE-CONTROL WIDTH CAN BE A SPEC LITERAL THAT OVERRIDES THE REFERENCE (R103, load-bearing).** **L03 fixes 180–210 ⇒ a 3-label control can never match a 4-label reference's pill width.**
70	- **WORD CENTRES BEAT CONTROL EDGES FOR A PITCH (R103, load-bearing).**
71	- **THE REFERENCE'S SEGMENTED CONTROL AND OURS SHARE ONE RADIUS TOKEN (R101–R104).** Ref lens **r ≈ 11.5 on h 24 (0.48)**; ref track **r ≈ 13.4–13.5**; ours **0.48 on both**.
72	- **A RADIUS IS MEASURED 1:1 AGAINST A SAME-HEIGHT ELEMENT, AND THE METHOD MUST RECOVER A KNOWN TOKEN FIRST (R101, load-bearing).** **threshold = the midpoint of THAT IMAGE's own two constants**; **only when the profile is monotone across the edge. R104: prefer the *within-image* track-vs-lens profile.**
73	- **A WHOLE-PAGE `ImageChops.difference` WITH A PER-ROW DIFF COUNT IS STILL THE CHEAPEST CONTAINMENT PROOF (R088).** Threshold **>6 RGB-sum**. **R109 used it to prove the `index > 0` guard is invisible: two captures differ by max 1/255 across the whole page.**
74	- **NEVER SCALE A REF *TYPE* ELEMENT BY THE WINDOW RATIO — FIND A SAME-CLASS INK IN BOTH IMAGES FIRST (R086).**
75	- **MEASURING A CORNER, A JOINT, A STRIPE, A BORDER OR AN INK (R075–R109).** Corner: per-row **fill-start inset** (body mode, R098; **interior rows, indexed from the first counted row, validated on a known token — R101/R102**; **R103: only on a monotone edge**; **R104: on a 250-on-255 fill use the rim's argmin core, and compare the outer element against the inner one in the SAME image**). Joint: per-row **`!= white` envelope**; **R107: a shared *horizontal* edge is separator-tone + the very next row's tone; R108: a shared *vertical* edge is the pair of fill edges plus whatever sits between them, and a JOIN must be read as an absolute tone against the fill (a translucent overlap reads DARKER, not lighter); R109: after the join, the acceptance is "the fill envelope is unbroken and contains no 255 and no rule tone".** Stripe: a saturated run whose **width is constant over the chip's full height**. Border: **monotonicity of a raw profile across an edge that abuts no rule**. Ink: the **per-channel coverage agreement test PLUS the channel-gap argument**; cross-capture: **top-5 %-coverage mean** and **`n<100`**; **R115: a glyph inside a disc/ring needs a ×6 zoom — thresholding the disc out of the plane does not threshold the digit out of the disc.** **Pitch: word centres, not edges (R103).**
76	- **HARNESS / COMMAND / TOKEN RULES.**
77	  **`captureClient` RETURNS `false` ON A NESTED RELATIVE PATH AND THE PNG IS SILENTLY NOT WRITTEN (R075).** Pass a **flat filename**; read the success flag in `live-runtime-vm.log`, then `ls` the actual CWD. **Pillow crops need ABSOLUTE paths** — the shell CWD moves between calls. **R107: our PNGs are written at zlib level 0 — three different captures share a byte size, so compare `md5sum`, never the size.**
78	  **THE LAUNCHER REFUSES WHEN A LIVED INSTANCE IS ALIVE (R079), AND `>/dev/null` HIDES IT.** `start-review-vm.sh` exits **1** with `Owned review instance still running: <pid>`. **ALWAYS `kill -0 $(cat live-app.pid)` FIRST: if the leg you need is already alive, the capture is FREE** (R114/R115 both took that path and touched nothing). **The R097–R109 working leg (ONE Bash call): kill `live-app.pid` → `nohup ./start-review-vm.sh light|dark &` → `sleep 38` → `python3 review-command.py '<json list>'` with `resize`/`sidebar`/`view`/`date`/`position`/`captureClient`/`stop` → grep `capture <name>.png true`.** **`review-command.py` IS NOT EXECUTABLE — always `python3 review-command.py`.**
79	  **HARNESS COMMAND FORM IS FLAT (R064).** `harness/Main.qml` matches `command.action` only; a command with no `action` **silently hits the fallback**. `review-command.py` takes **ONE argv that is a JSON list**, bumps `sequence` itself, writes **in place** (never `os.replace`), and **sleeps 0.6 s between commands**. A rebuilt binary needs a **kill+relaunch** (**~38 s to a usable state**). Include `resize 1100x692`; the app starts in `--view week --date 2026-10-15` **with the sidebar COLLAPSED**. **The theme is fixed at launch — a dark leg costs a full kill+relaunch.** Only `date`/`position`/`wheel`/`flick`/`stop`/`openItem{kind,titleContains}`/`windowWheel` are available: **`hovered`/`pressed` chrome cannot be driven, and a static screenshot can never settle an animation.**
80	  **Compositing (R077/R080/R088/R097/R099/R101–R109/R115).** **A composite (a 1:1 strip above a 2–4× zoom) answers "overall form + local detail" in ONE image read**, and **labelling the rows (`ImageDraw.text`) is what makes it self-describing.** **`LANCZOS` for a ×1.8 upscale of a ref crop; `NEAREST` when the point is pixel structure.** **Captions go on the FINAL canvas at 1x — text drawn *before* an ×N upscale is illegible, and the canvas height must include the caption block.** **R109: side-by-side panel captions collide even at 615 px of canvas — stack caption LINES, one per panel, at full width. R115: a 1:1 ref strip beside three ×6 zooms needs `W = 12 + stripW + 16 + zoomW*3 + 16`; +12 px per zoom tile is enough gutter.** **No `numpy` here.**
81	  **A WIDE, SHALLOW CROP CANNOT BE READ AT ×5+ (R107).** **Crop to the feature (≤30 rows) and anchor on the feature.**
82	  **`tmp/` is gitignored.** The committable artifact is the mirror under **`docs/ui-calendar/`**: copy screenshots in (name them **`r0NN-<slug>.png`**) and **prepend** the round summary to `docs/ui-calendar/LEDGER.md` (newest first) — **prepend with `Path.write_text(entry + old)`; an `Edit` whose only `old_string` is the previous round's heading deletes that heading.** `state.md`/`rounds.md` can never be committed — expected. **Commits must end with the `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5` trailer.** **A `python3 -c` whose payload contains markdown backticks is mangled by the shell — write the payload to a file and use a heredoc.**

## 外推待确认 (live only — older live items are archived to rounds.md tail)
- **THE MINI MONTH'S GRID IS MONTH-INDEPENDENT (R115, load-bearing).** The six date-band tops are **561/582/603/624/645/666** — identical in the Apr-2026 capture (R112/R114) and the Oct-2026 one (R115) — and the disc overhangs its 9-row band by **4 above / 2 below** in both. A mini-month reading taken on one month therefore holds for any month.
- **A 9-ROW GLYPH INSIDE A 15 px RING IS NOT LEGIBLE ENOUGH TO CARRY A TONE CLAIM (R115, load-bearing).** R112/R114 read the selection disc's digit as "the ordinary text tone" at 1:1; the **×6 zoom** shows it is `(63,63,66)` against in-month **~216–220**. **Ring/disc interiors need a zoom before any tone claim** — a threshold that separates the ring from the plane will not separate the digit from the ring.
- **THE CLAUSE AND THE REFERENCE CAN DISAGREE ON A SIZE (R115, load-bearing).** M04 says the today circle is **18–20**; the ref's is **15 at 1:1** and **17.3** in our layout (scale 1.155, derived two ways). **When a spec literal is not the reference at any measurable scale, the literal wins by default but the ref numbers must be recorded beside it** — the ruling is not ours to make.
- **THE SIDEBAR'S 1 px RIM AT x220 EXISTS ON BOTH LEGS (R114, load-bearing).** Dark `(53,53,53)` at x220 with the plane 40 at x219; light `(224,224,224)` with the plane 228. **A whole-sidebar ink scan must stop at x219:** over x0..**220** the dark leg returns a single band (490,691) because every row contains the rim, while the light leg's rim is only 4 tones off the plane and hides under a threshold of 8. **A whole-sidebar test that passes on light can be silently vacuous on dark — always name the x range and check the rim.**
- **THE MINI MONTH HAS NO FILL OF ITS OWN (R114, load-bearing).** The block's field IS the sidebar plane ((40,40,40) dark / 228 light, the dominant tone in **every** row of the block), so **M01's 12 / 12 margins are arithmetic, not tonal**: they follow from `cellWidth 196/7 = 28.0` and the column centres 26.0 + 28.0i (=> cells 12..208 in a 220 px sidebar) and can never be read off a fill edge. - **A PIXEL RUN p..q IS THE HALF-OPEN INTERVAL [p, q+1) — ITS CENTRE IS (p+q+1)/2 (R112, load-bearing calibration).** The inclusive form `(p+q)/2` shifts every centre 0.5 px left; on the mini month it produced margins **11.5 / 12.5** where the layout can only have equal ones (`Main.qml:2122-2123` sets the *same* `categoryInset` on both sides).
